Hildegard 0.1.5 is a pre-alpha. From this release on, Hildegard and its apps update themselves.

## Install

- **macOS and Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Desktop app:** pick your system's download below, or from [dbaney.com/hildegard](https://dbaney.com/hildegard/).

Installed already? Run the line above once more, or download the app again: this is the last time you'll need to.

## New

- **Hildegard updates itself.** Every six hours it looks for a new release. When one is out and nothing is rendering or downloading, it installs it and starts again as the new version, keeping the one before. Choose when instead in Settings › About (**Ask me first**), or with `hildegard update auto off`; then `hildegard update` or **Update** in Settings when you want it.
- **The desktop apps update themselves** on macOS, Windows and Linux (the AppImage). A new app downloads in the background, and **Restart to update** appears at the top of the tray menu. The .deb doesn't update itself yet.
- **Every update is signed.** The apps and `hildegard update` refuse anything not signed with Hildegard's key, and refuse an older release passed off as a new one.
- **The Omarchy panel** offers **Update to** a new release, and says when Hildegard is updating.

## Known limits

- Macs don't render on their own GPU yet. Pair a Mac with a computer that has an NVIDIA or AMD GPU
  (`hildegard choir join`).
- The Windows and macOS apps aren't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask you to confirm the first launch.
- Hildegard Link, the encrypted relay for reaching Hildegard without Tailscale, is a prototype and not switched on yet.
- LTX models follow Lightricks' license: free under $10M yearly revenue, and not for products that compete with
  Lightricks. Wan 2.2 is Apache-2.0.
